The story relies heavily on well-worn romantic drama clichés and tropes. The setting (a rainy harbor café), the physical actions (keeping a coat on to signal emotional distance and then unbuttoning it to show a slight softening, staring out the window, clinking a spoon against porcelain during an awkward silence), and the dialogue ("Do you remember that summer at the lake?", "You look good", and the metaphor "The mail was never the problem") are all overused conventions in stories about estranged former lovers reuniting. Because these elements are so familiar and predictable, the piece lacks originality.
